lines.trans: You're selling quite a random assortment of things. You seem to have fallen pretty far.

words.gram: Contracted progressive てる-form of 売る (to sell).

lines.trans: If that's how it looks, I suppose so. Even so, I'm alive—I haven't gone wrong.
What about the people dragged down with you? This time, I won't forgive you.
Toshi killed Furuya—he stormed into Furuya's office all by himself.
You understand what kind of resolve that took, don't you? He put your life ahead of his own!

words.gram: Past tense of plain copula だ.

lines.trans: Nobody can resist your magnetism—even to the point of choosing his own death.
Wait—please stop...

words.gram: Plain imperative of くれる (give/do for me).

lines.trans: He was the one and only man who kept accepting you unconditionally all the way through.
He never once turned his back on you, did he?
Do things your own way, boss! Let's grab big money and rise to the top!

words.gloss: rise from the bottom to riches

lines.trans: In the end, he was the one who held everything together. So at the very least, live like yourself, Mr. Muranishi.

words.gram: Plain imperative of くれる (give/do for me).

lines.trans: What Toshi loved was who you were as a director.

meanings.note: て-form 売って links 'sell' into the next action.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: 売ってる物がバラバラなんですね。随分落ちぶれたようで。
examples.trans: You're selling quite a random assortment of things. You seem to have fallen pretty far.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。
売ってる物がバラバラなんですね。随分落ちぶれたようで。
examples.trans: You're selling quite a random assortment of things. You seem to have fallen pretty far.

examples.text: 荒波にもまれて方々にぶつかって、なめられてできたこのきれいなフォルム、非常にセクシーでございましょ？
examples.trans: Tossed by rough waves and licked smooth millions of times into this lovely form—isn't it remarkably sexy?

meanings.note: Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

examples.trans: I see that to be seen.

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

meanings.en: and so; because of that; with that
meanings.note: Conjunction indicating a result or asking 'and then what happened?'.

examples.text: それでどうなりましたか。
それで問題が解決しました。
examples.trans: With that, the problem was solved.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: そんなことしたら世の中がめちゃくちゃになりますよ！
examples.trans: If you aired things like that on television, society would fall apart!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Refers to humans in general or human nature.

examples.text: 人間には表と裏がある。
examples.trans: Human beings have a public face and a hidden side.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Read ひと when standing as an independent noun.

examples.text: 親切な人に会いました。
みんな乗り込むよ。忘れ物ないようにね。
examples.trans: Everyone hop in the van. Make sure nobody leaves anything behind.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Combines どう (how) + いう (say); どういうこと means 'what does this mean?'.

examples.trans: What is the meaning of this?

meanings.note: Mental readiness to face something difficult or risky.

examples.text: この世界に入る覚悟はあるのか？
examples.trans: Are you prepared to enter this world?

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Casual, blunt contraction of あなた used between intimates or in heated speech.

examples.text: エクスタシーを優先させればいいんですわ。ありのままで挑めば大丈夫ですよ。
examples.trans: Simply put ecstasy first. If you face it just as you are, you will be fine.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Reflexive pronoun pointing back to the person under discussion.

examples.text: 自分の言葉で話します。
examples.trans: I speak in my own words.

meanings.note: Godan verb; past tense is 死んだ.

examples.text: 金魚が死んでしまった。

examples.trans: I don't want to die yet.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。
選んでくださり、ありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you very much for selecting me.

examples.text: あら、じゃあわたくしのも選んでいただこうかしら。広告のお仕事がありますの。
examples.trans: Oh my, then perhaps I'll ask you to pick something for me too. I have an ad shoot coming up.

meanings.en: nothing more than (after past verb); up to
meanings.note: After a plain verb + です (出店したまでです), modestly states 'we simply did that and nothing more'.

examples.text: 念のため聞いたまでです。
examples.trans: I merely asked just in case.

meanings.note: て-form 待って + ください is 'please wait'; causative お待たせして means 'having kept you waiting'.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

examples.text: あいつはね、あなたのことをずーっと受け入れ続けたたった一人の男ですよ。
examples.trans: He was the one and only man who kept accepting you unconditionally all the way through.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

examples.text: あいつからあんたのことを拒んだことないだろ。
examples.trans: He never once turned his back on you, did he?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Na-adjective; the thing liked is marked with が or は.

examples.text: どんな食べ物が好きですか。
examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。
おっさんが好きなようにやりゃいいんだよ。ビッグマネーつかんで成り上がるんだよ！
examples.trans: Do things your own way, boss! Let's grab big money and rise to the top!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: rise from the bottom to riches

examples.text: おっさんが好きなようにやりゃいいんだよ。ビッグマネーつかんで成り上がるんだよ！
examples.trans: Do things your own way, boss! Let's grab big money and rise to the top!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: With で (全部で), means 'in total' or 'altogether'.

meanings.en: in the end; after all; ultimately
meanings.note: Used when summing up what a situation comes down to.

examples.text: 結局、金がないと自由にもなれないんだな。
examples.trans: In the end, without money, you can't even be free.

examples.text: 結局、彼には会えませんでした。
examples.trans: In the end, I couldn't meet him.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Evidential auxiliary adjective expressing hearsay or inference.

examples.text: 百万冊以上売れてるらしい。
examples.trans: Apparently it sells over a million copies.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Standard polite 'goodbye'.
